gap: No result ChatGPT cited states which kit carries the Apple pentalobe bits or whether the driver runs on the charge cable. The only result that says so is Fanttik's uncited E1 MAX troubleshooting guide, which appeared in one of the seven result sets. It says the E1 MAX's 50-bit set includes Pentalobe P2 and P5 and Torx T5, the case label gives bit numbers for iPhone, MacBook, Joy-Con and PS5, and the E1 MAX keeps driving while charging but the E2 Ultra cannot be used while charging.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rivals: Fanttik's 'HOTO vs Fanttik' guide and its 'E1 vs E2' guide. Both give only bit counts ('50 S2 magnetic bits' each for E1 MAX and E2 Ultra) and no bit profiles, bit-to-device pairings or charging behaviour. I could not open the cited E1 MAX product page because it returned HTTP 429 every time, so I cannot say what it lacks. Among the uncited top results, toolengineers.com gives no shank size, bit list or device list for any pick. butactuallygood.com gives 5/32-in. hex bits for the E1 Max and E2 Ultra but mentions no pentalobe bits for any product. ChatGPT already told shoppers that the iFixit driver takes 4 mm bits, comes without bits and runs on AAA batteries. The pentalobe and use-while-charging facts appear only in Fanttik's own troubleshooting guide, which ChatGPT got once and never cited, so they are only partly new.
decides: It supports the E1 MAX as the pick for phone and MacBook work, because Fanttik names Pentalobe P2 and P5 bits in its kit and labels them for iPhone and MacBook. ChatGPT pushed the E2 Ultra as the 'versatile' upgrade, but I could not source a pentalobe bit in the E2 Ultra kit, and Fanttik's guide says it cannot be used while charging. Do not present the E2 Ultra as a drop-in for iPhone or MacBook screws until its bit map is sourced. The iFixit driver is the budget choice only for shoppers who already own 4 mm bits.
